content.title: Full-stack engineer · Lagos / remote
content.tagline: I build server-rendered products that stay fast under real traffic.
content.bio: Eight years across checkout, dispatch and internal tooling. I work close to the render path — measuring before rewriting, and shipping the smallest change that moves the number. Currently leading the front-end platform team at Ledgerwork.

items.title: Ledgerwork checkout
items.problem: A five-step checkout lost buyers at every hop, and the client-side bundle blocked first paint on mid-range Android.
items.solution: Rebuilt it as one server-rendered page with progressive enhancement, so the form works before any JavaScript runs.
items.impact: Completion up 14 points; median load 2.4s to 880ms.
items.role: I architected the render path and the payment-state machine, and paired with two engineers on the form components.

bodies.business:
A five-step checkout lost buyers at every hop, and the client-side bundle blocked first paint on mid-range Android. Support tickets clustered on the payment step, where a failed card silently reset the form.

  • Median load 2.4s, worst case over 6s on 3G
  • Drop-off of 31% between address and payment
  • No recovery path once a payment errored
bodies.solution:
Rebuilt it as one server-rendered page with progressive enhancement, so the form works before any JavaScript runs. Payment state moved server-side, which made errors recoverable rather than destructive.

  • Single POST target with per-field server validation
  • Hotwire frames for the address lookup, optional by design
  • Idempotent payment intents keyed to the cart
bodies.role:
I architected the render path and the payment-state machine end to end, then paired with two engineers on the form components.

  • Owned the performance budget and the regression gate in CI
  • Wrote the migration plan that let the old flow run in parallel for six weeks
  • Ran the rollout, including the rollback we needed on day two

items.title: Beacon design system
items.problem: Nine product teams shipped four incompatible button implementations and no shared token source.
items.solution: 62 framework-agnostic components on one token pipeline, adopted incrementally with no migration freeze.
items.impact: Adopted by all nine teams in seven months; UI review time down by half.
items.role: I owned the token pipeline and the release process, and wrote the contribution model the teams still use.

bodies.business:
Nine product teams shipped four incompatible button implementations and no shared token source. Every visual change meant nine tickets, and accessibility fixes landed in one product and nowhere else.

  • No single source of truth for colour or spacing
  • UI review was the slowest stage in every release
bodies.solution:
62 framework-agnostic components on one token pipeline, adopted incrementally with no migration freeze.

  • Tokens compiled from one JSON source to CSS, iOS and Android
  • Components shipped as web components, usable from React and Vue
  • Visual regression suite gating every release
bodies.role:
I owned the token pipeline and the release process, and wrote the contribution model the teams still use.

  • Set the versioning and deprecation policy
  • Ran a weekly office hour for adopting teams

items.title: Freight ops console

screenshot.alt: The dispatch console on a tablet.

items.problem: Dispatchers ran 400 daily routes from a spreadsheet, on tablets that lose signal inside the yard.
items.solution: Offline-first console with a local write queue and conflict review, keyboard-first for one-handed use.
items.impact: Route assignment down from 6 minutes to 40 seconds per load.
items.role: I built the sync layer and the conflict-resolution UI; the mapping integration was a colleague's.

bodies.business:
Dispatchers ran 400 daily routes from a spreadsheet, on tablets that lose signal inside the yard. A lost connection meant re-entering an hour of assignments.

  • Assignment took roughly 6 minutes per load
  • No audit trail when two dispatchers edited the same route
bodies.solution:
An offline-first console with a local write queue and conflict review, keyboard-first for one-handed use beside a truck.

  • Writes queue locally and replay on reconnect
  • Conflicts surface as a side-by-side review, never a silent overwrite
  • Every action reachable without the touch keyboard
bodies.role:
I built the sync layer and the conflict-resolution UI. The mapping integration was a colleague's work.

  • Designed the write-queue schema and replay ordering
  • Shadowed two dispatch shifts before writing any code

items.title: Council records search

screenshot.alt: A search result page of council minutes.

items.problem: A city of 1.2M published two decades of minutes as unsearchable scanned PDFs.
items.solution: Full-text search over an OCR pipeline, with result pages that work in a screen reader and on a 2G connection.
items.impact: 31,000 documents indexed; tested end to end with two local advocacy groups.
items.role: I designed the index schema and the search UI, and ran the accessibility testing sessions.

bodies.business:
A city of 1.2M published two decades of minutes as unsearchable scanned PDFs. Residents and journalists had no way to find a decision without knowing its date.

  • ~31,000 documents, image-only, no text layer
  • Existing portal unusable with a screen reader
bodies.solution:
Full-text search over an OCR pipeline, with result pages that work in a screen reader and on a 2G connection.

  • Tesseract pipeline with per-page confidence scoring
  • Postgres full-text ranking, tuned on real query logs
  • Server-rendered results, under 30KB per page
bodies.role:
I designed the index schema and the search UI, and ran the accessibility testing sessions myself.

  • Two rounds of moderated testing with local advocacy groups
  • Wrote the public documentation for the data export

items.title: Shift planner (retail client)
items.problem: Managers built weekly rotas for hourly staff across six separate forms, and overtime went unnoticed until payroll.
items.solution: One editable weekly grid with live cost and overtime totals, validated server-side against local labour rules.
items.impact: Rota build time cut from ~2 hours to 25 minutes per store.
items.role: I owned the scheduling rules engine and the cost calculations end to end.

bodies.business:
Managers built weekly rotas for hourly staff across six separate forms, and overtime went unnoticed until payroll closed.

  • Rota build took roughly 2 hours per store
  • Overtime breaches found weeks after the fact
bodies.solution:
One editable weekly grid with live cost and overtime totals, validated server-side against local labour rules.

  • Totals recompute per cell edit, server-authoritative
  • Rule violations block save with a plain-language reason
bodies.role:
I owned the scheduling rules engine and the cost calculations end to end.

  • Encoded the labour rules with the client's compliance lead
  • Built the reconciliation report payroll now runs weekly
